scenes.line1: How do you change data safely?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how you can update your data structure in Kafka without breaking everything? Let’s find out.

scenes.label: Registry
scenes.sub: Stores and manages schemas for Kafka topics.
scenes.say: A schema registry is where you store and manage your data schemas for Kafka topics. It keeps everyone on the same page.

rows.b: Add your schema to the registry

scenes.say: First, you register your schema. When you need to update it, you change the fields, then check for compatibility to avoid breaking things.
Backward compatibility means old data still works with new code. Forward compatibility means new data works with old code. Both help prevent data corruption.

scenes.question: What if you skip compatibility checks?
scenes.wrong: It just adds new fields safely.
scenes.right: You risk breaking consumers and corrupting data.
scenes.say: Here’s a common trap: skipping compatibility checks. That can break your consumers or even corrupt your data.
